name: Frog Prince

items.name: Watery Demesne
items.text: The frog prince designates an unclaimed body of water (typically a pond) to become his demesne. While in his demesne, the frog prince can speak and gains a +15-foot status bonus to all his Speeds. If the frog prince dies or finds a new demesne, the waters turn murky and putrid for 1 week before returning to normal as it ceases to be his demesne.

items.name: How Dare You!
items.text:
Trigger A creature misses a Strike against the frog prince

---
Effect The frog prince makes a melee Strike against the triggering creature if it's within range.

items.name: Princely Monologue
items.text:
Requirements The frog prince is in his watery demesne

---
Effect The frog prince enraptures all those who play audience to his speech. Each creature in a 60-foot emanation must attempt a DC 21 Will save saving throw. The monologue lasts until the end of the frog prince's next turn, but he can Sustain it for up to 10 minutes. Each time he Sustains the monologue, any creature in the area who hasn't already attempted a saving throw against Princely Monologue must attempt the saving throw.

---
Critical Success The creature is unaffected and becomes temporarily immune to Princely Monologue for 1 hour.

Success The creature is Fascinated with the frog prince, but only for 1 round.

Failure The creature is fascinated with the frog prince and can't willingly move away from the frog prince while it can hear the Princely Monologue.

Critical Failure As failure, except the creature is also Stupefied 2 while it can hear the frog prince's Princely Monologue.

items.name: True Love's Bond
items.text:
Frequency once per year

Trigger A humanoid creature who truly loves the frog prince kisses him

---
Effect The frog prince permanently transforms into a Small or Medium humanoid. He chooses his ancestry and the details of his appearance, and his equipment changes to suit his new form. The frog prince loses the fey trait and gains the humanoid trait. He has a land Speed of 25 feet and loses his swim Speed. He can use his rapier and water jet Strikes as normal. If the GM determines the humanoid creature's feelings aren't true love, this ability has no effect.

text: Lo and behold the tale of the frog prince, often depicted as a lost royal transformed by vile machinations. His daring, amphibious exploits are all in search of the destined love who'll elevate him to his true form and his rightful place upon the throne—or so it goes. When such stories persist in a region, whether as folk tales about a nearby pond or as placation for excitable children before bedtime, the innocent belief in their plight seemingly invokes an inexplicable, ancient power that gives form to frog princes. These fey appear as unusually large frogs, gifted with a capacity for expression atypical for most amphibians.
